q2_gaps: attributive "a similar N" with an elided standard of comparison: the Symmetric section covers only the copular "X is similar to Y", so recovering the anaphoric second argument is unspecified

a bare plural count noun as the object of an oblique preposition ("in Pakistani blocks"): the oblique object-NP rule covers an article-marked NP (witness with its kind atom) and a bare mass/domain/proper name (constant), but not a bare plural count noun, which here needed a group witness

a fronted purpose/framing PP on an existential clause ("For shopping, there is ..."): it fits either the noun-complement For rule, which would reify the clausal gerund, or the framing/domain oblique, which keeps a bare constant, and nothing selects between them
notes: "in Pakistani blocks" was attached to the second market only (minimal attachment); the alternative wide attachment is available, but the text is Tier-C-garbled, which the multiple-readings section excludes from multi-reading emission. Nationality-adjective fusion (russian_market, pakistani_block) with the predicable-modifier genus follows the breton_tapestry line, and the two indefinites correctly take distinct witnesses.
